subject: history
title: Building the British Empire Adventure
welcome_lead: How did Britain end up ruling a quarter of the world? Let's trace the rise of the British Empire. 🌍
meta_desc: British Empire Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of how Britain built the largest empire in history.
final_note: You saw how trade, the navy and force built the Empire, and learned the meaning of 'colony' and 'empire'.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An empire is when one country rules over many others.

A country ruled by another is called a colony. By 1900, Britain had colonies on every continent and the British Empire covered about a quarter of the world's land and people.

People said 'the sun never set' on it, because somewhere in the Empire it was always daytime. ☀️

Three main things built the Empire:

  • Trade — Britain wanted spices, sugar, cotton, tea and tobacco.
  • The Royal Navy — the strongest navy in the world protected ships and ports.
  • Force — Britain often used soldiers to take or hold land.

The East India Company was a private firm that ended up ruling much of India for the king. After 1858 the British government took over directly — the British Raj.

Key colonies included:

  • India — 'the jewel in the crown'
  • Canada, Australia, New Zealand — settler colonies
  • Caribbean islands — sugar plantations
  • African colonies — mainly from the late 1800s

The Empire brought wealth to Britain, but it took freedom, land and lives from millions of people around the world.
